title: Neither Neighbours nor Partners
statement: How many subsets of $\{1, 2, \dots, 14\}$, including the empty set, contain no two consecutive integers and no two integers whose sum is $15$?
hints: Draw a graph on the numbers $1, \dots, 14$, joining two numbers when they cannot both be in the subset. Place each $k$ next to $15 - k$.
The graph is a ladder whose $7$ rungs are the pairs $\{k, 15 - k\}$. Count its independent sets one rung at a time, keeping track of whether the last rung is empty or which of its ends is chosen.
solution:
Join two numbers when they cannot both be chosen. The edges are $\{k, k + 1\}$ for $1 \le k \le 13$ and $\{k, 15 - k\}$ for $1 \le k \le 7$, and $\{7, 8\}$ is in both lists. So the graph is a ladder with rails $1, 2, \dots, 7$ and $14, 13, \dots, 8$ and rungs $\{k, 15 - k\}$, and we need its independent sets.

For the first $n$ rungs, let $e_n$ count the independent sets with rung $n$ empty and $f_n$ those using one end of rung $n$. Then $e_n = e_{n-1} + f_{n-1}$. A chosen end of rung $n$ allows rung $n - 1$ to be empty or to use its other end, so $f_n = 2e_{n-1} + f_{n-1}$. Starting from $(e_1, f_1) = (1, 2)$, the pairs are $(3, 4)$, $(7, 10)$, $(17, 24)$, $(41, 58)$, $(99, 140)$ and $(239, 338)$. The answer is $239 + 338 = 577$.
